newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian PM sees Telstra vote in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian PM sees Telstra vote in two weeks.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday he expected the upper house of parliament, the Senate, to vote on the government's plan to sell one-third of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp in the next couple of weeks.
But Howard said he was still unsure whether the Senate would approve the plan.
"In the next couple of weeks, there'll be a crucial vote on the Telstra legislation," Howard said on Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
The government needs the support of Independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston to pass the legislation in the non-government dominated Senate.
The Labor opposition, the Australian Democrats and the Greens minor party are all opposed to the sale.
Howard said negotiations were continuing with both Harradine and Colston.
"I honestly don't know (if the legislation will be passed) at this stage," he said.
"The relevant minister (Communications Minister Richard Alston) is still discussing the matter with the relevant senators who hold the balance of power.
"We have to do that -- they haven't signed off on it, so to speak, in entirety."
Howard said the government's budget would be hard hit if the Telstra bill and a number of other contentious budget measures failed to pass the Senate.
"If they don't go through, then there will have been a very heavy hit made by the Senate on the bottom line of the budget," he said.
"Nobody should be in any doubt about that," Howard said.

Other key budget measures scheduled to be voted on in the Senate in the next two weeks include the research and development tax break legislation and the higher education legislative amendment bill, which is due to be voted on later today.
The conservative Liberal-National government plans to raise A$8 billion from the partial sale of Telstra, with A$1 billion earmarked for an environment package.
